ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the top of the figure is an acyl/aroyloxy fragment: R–C(=O)–O–C(=O)– connected to a benzene ring bearing three Cl substituents; there are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Below is a dimethylaminopyridine fragment: the ring nitrogen on the pyridine ring points toward the upper carbonyl in a dashed-line/interaction manner, and the para position of the ring is connected to an N(CH3)2 substituent. Reasoning: Count by fragments and exclude all bonds involving hydrogen. In the upper fragment, the non-hydrogen skeleton bonds of R–C(=O)–O–C(=O)–aryl are 6; inside the benzene ring there are 6 ring bonds; the three C–Cl substituent bonds are 3. Therefore the upper part has 6 + 6 + 3 = 15 in total. In the lower dimethylaminopyridine fragment, inside the pyridine ring there are 6 ring bonds; the bond from the ring to the external amino N is 1; the bonds from this N to the two methyl groups are 2. Therefore the lower part has 6 + 1 + 2 = 9 in total. The total is 15 + 9 = 24 bonds.

method.method_draft: Count by fragments. For the upper fragment, count 6 acyclic bonds in R–C(=O)–O–C(=O)–aryl, plus 6 bonds in the benzene ring, plus 3 C–Cl substituent bonds, giving 15. For the lower dimethylaminopyridine fragment, count 6 ring bonds, plus 1 ring–N substituent bond, plus 2 N–methyl bonds, giving 9. Add all components: 15 + 9 = 24.
